262.body: Session listing capped at 50 was truncating large orgs without any hint that more existed. IdentityService now returns a next-page token and issue_refresh_token plus verify_refresh_token are untouched. Clients that ignore the token get exactly what they got before. Testing: paged through a 200-session fixture.
262.title: identity-api: paginate session listing

263.body: The refund() handler accepted a full refund for an order that was already partially refunded, as long as each request stayed under the order total. Support hit this twice and had to claw money back manually. refund() now sums prior refunds for the order and rejects anything that would push the total over. Partial-refund math for the happy path is unchanged. Testing: added over-refund regression tests covering partial-then-full sequences.
263.title: payments-api: block over-refunds in refund handler

264.body: Cart.clear now also resets the applied promo code instead of leaving it attached to the empty cart. Shoppers who cleared their cart and started over kept the old promo, which then failed confusingly at checkout when it no longer applied!! new_cart and get_cart are untouched. The Cart model drops the code in the same write that drops the items. Testing: added clear-with-promo cases.
264.title: cart: clear promo code in Cart.clear

265.body: The confirmation page now shows the estimated delivery window next to each shipment group. render_checkout reads the window from the shipping options we already fetch, so no new requests. Groups without a window show nothing rather than a placeholder. Testing: checked single-group, multi-group, and no-window carts on staging.
265.title: web-frontend: show delivery windows on confirmation

266.body: ledger storage autoscaling enabled. was manual. one less 3am page.
266.title: postgres-ledger: enable storage autoscaling

267.body: weekend failover test passed. replica promoted in 4 min, app reconnected clean. no changes needed, recording the result.
267.title: postgres-payments: weekend failover drill results

268.body: post_entry now attaches the caller name to every entry it writes, so the audit view can show who originated each line instead of just the service name. LedgerEntry carries the new field end to end, and old entries read back with an empty caller. Testing: wrote entries from two callers and confirmed the audit view distinguishes them.
268.title: ledger: record caller name in post_entry

269.body: The order summary now collapses gift options behind a disclosure instead of showing them always. Most shoppers never gift-wrap, and the section pushed the total below the fold on small screens!! render_checkout keeps the state per session, and WebFrontend remembers the last choice. Testing: checked expanded, collapsed, and remembered states on mobile widths.
269.title: web-frontend: collapse gift options in render_checkout

270.body: slow query threshold lowered to 250ms on payments. caught two bad queries already. dashboards updated.
270.title: postgres-payments: lower slow-query threshold

271.body: is_enabled now logs every flag evaluation at debug level with the subject id and result. Debugging rollout issues used to mean guessing, because the only signal was behavior. FeatureFlagService batches the log writes so hot paths are unaffected, and set_flag is unchanged. Testing: enabled debug logging on staging and confirmed evaluations appear with correct results.
271.title: feature-flags: debug logging for is_enabled

272.body: place_order now passes a request id into with_retry so the checkout logs and the app logs can be correlated for a single order. Previously the two sides logged independently and matching them up during incidents was manual grep work. with_retry accepts an optional label parameter and includes it in its attempt logs; CheckoutService generates the id. Behavior on success and failure is unchanged. Testing: placed orders on staging and confirmed both sides share the id.
272.title: checkout: correlate place_order logs with request id

273.body: ledger backups encrypted at rest now. were plaintext snapshots. compliance will be happy 🔒
273.title: postgres-ledger: encrypt ledger backups

274.body: maintenance window moved to sunday 4am. was saturday noon, overlapped with peak traffic. moved.
274.title: postgres-main: move maintenance window

275.body: read replica added in second AZ. failover now automatic. tested, works.
275.title: postgres-main: add cross-AZ read replica

276.body: AuthService.login now locks the account for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts instead of letting attempts continue forever. Support saw brute-force noise weekly and the only defense was the global rate limit. The lockout counter resets on success and the error tells the user when to try again. Testing: covered lockout, reset-on-success, and expiry.
276.title: auth: lock accounts after repeated login failures

277.body: list_products now filters out-of-stock products by default, with an include_unavailable flag for the merchandising views that need them. The storefront was showing products nobody could buy, and the bounce rate on those pages was terrible. get_product still returns individual products regardless of stock. Testing: added default-filter and flag-on cases.
277.title: catalog: hide out-of-stock products in list_products

278.body: redis persistence turned on (RDB snapshots every 15 min). a restart used to wipe everything and cause a thundering herd on the db. snapshots now cover us 📸
278.title: redis-cache: enable RDB persistence

279.body: log retention extended to 30 days. support needed older logs for a dispute. done.
279.title: postgres-main: extend log retention

280.body: WebFrontend now sets a proper page title per checkout step ('Shipping', 'Payment', 'Review') instead of the generic app name on every step. Small thing, but support calls about 'which step am I on' should drop. render_checkout notifies the shell on step change. Testing: stepped through checkout on staging and confirmed titles.
280.title: web-frontend: per-step page titles in checkout

281.body: check_limit now returns the seconds until reset alongside the RateLimited error, so clients can back off intelligently instead of hammering. dispatch() passes the value through from the limiter. RateLimited carries a retry_after field and reset() semantics are unchanged. Testing: asserted the header value matches the limiter state in the route tests.
281.title: api-gateway: expose rate-limit reset time

282.body: Rate limit headers are now consistent across all routes. Some returned Retry-After, some didn't. dispatch() normalizes them. Clients can rely on the header now.
282.title: api-gateway: normalize rate-limit headers

283.body: performance insights retention set to 7 days. was 24h, too short for weekly comparisons. changed.
283.title: postgres-payments: extend insights retention

284.body: save() now stamps every outbox row with the originating service name so relay() logs can say where each entry came from. Debugging cross-service ordering issues used to start with guesswork. LedgerEntry and post_entry pass the name through, FakeBus ignores it, and publish() includes it in the relayed metadata. Testing: multi-service ordering test asserts the stamp survives the relay.
284.title: ledger: stamp outbox rows with origin service

285.body: check_limit now exempts the health-check endpoint from rate limiting. The load balancer probes were eating into the request budget and tripped RateLimited twice during deploys. dispatch() short-circuits /health before the limiter, and reset() is unchanged. Testing: hammered /health during a deploy on staging, zero 429s.
285.title: api-gateway: exempt health checks from rate limits

295.body: charge() now validates the currency code against the supported list before contacting the provider, raising immediately on unknown codes. A typo ('UDS') last month produced a confusing provider error three layers deep. StripeClient holds the allowlist and __init__ lets tests inject extras. Testing: added bad-currency cases for all three providers.
295.title: stripe-adapter: validate currency codes in charge

296.body: issue_refresh_token now embeds the client version in the token metadata so verify_refresh_token can apply version-specific validation. Old app versions send slightly different payloads and the server kept guessing. Tokens without a version behave exactly as before. Testing: issued tokens from three client versions and verified each validates.
296.title: identity-api: tag tokens with client version

297.body: ConnectionPool.acquire now records the wait time on every acquisition, not just when it exceeds the old warn threshold, so the latency dashboards finally have the full distribution. get_pool and reset_pool are untouched, and run_query reports the same shape as before. This only adds measurement — no behavior change underneath. Testing: asserted wait samples appear for fast and slow acquisitions in the updated suite.
297.title: payments-api: record pool wait times on every acquire

298.body: reserve() now returns the reservation expiry timestamp so the frontend can show a countdown instead of letting the hold silently lapse!! Previously shoppers learned their hold expired only at checkout, which felt like a bug. InventoryService computes the expiry from the existing TTL config. Testing: added expiry-present and expiry-sane assertions.
298.title: inventory: return reservation expiry from reserve
